methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: Animatronics, AI and more at Virginia Tech’s Music + Technology Festival
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's AI music festival and Roanoke College's partnership with Google for free AI training certificates signal peer-driven knowledge networks and accessible upskilling outside traditional tech hubs, demonstrating distributed capability-building through educational institutions in mid-sized regions.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: A Norfolk native bringing free AI workshops to Hampton Roads explicitly targets closing the technology gap, representing grassroots, community-driven AI literacy efforts that could enable distributed deep learning rather than platform-dependent shallow adoption.

signals.title: NoVA Leaders Debate Data Centers, Metro Funding And The Housing Crisis - Patch
signals.signal_reading: NoVA leaders debating data center proliferation, Metro funding, and housing crisis reveals how AI infrastructure concentration creates regional wealth and governance capacity that diverges from the rest of Virginia, deepening metro advantages while other regions lack similar policy leverage.

signals.title: Virginia should make AI adoption strengthen the career ladder | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: A guest column advocating that Virginia ensure AI adoption strengthens career ladders suggests concern that platform-delivered AI tools may hollow out middle-skill work rather than building deep capability, signaling tension between accessibility and meaningful skill development across the state.

signals.title: Andrea Fletcher tapped to lead Virginia’s government technology overhaul
signals.signal_reading: Appointing a leader for Virginia's government technology overhaul centralizes AI governance capacity in Richmond, potentially concentrating technical decision-making authority rather than distributing implementation capability to regional and local government operations statewide.
